newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM palladium prices tumble, gold firmer.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM palladium prices tumble, gold firmer.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo palladium prices ended sharply lower on Monday in a correction to recent overbought conditions, while gold futures ended marginally firmer, traders said.
Most palladium futures tumbled by their 22 yen per gram daily limit. Benchmark December fell by 22 yen to 525 yen.

"Palladium futures were under heavy selling pressure, with bearish sentiment carried over from last Friday," one trader said. "A correction may continue. But bullish sentiment remains intact until the exact time schedule of the Japan-Russia export talks on platinum group metals is set," the trader said.
Spot palladium was quoted at $131.50/132.50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, after opening at $133.50/134.50.

The trader said the spot price may dip to around $130 per ounce in the near-term, but any further losses would be limited as the global palladium market, especially sponge grade which is mainly used in catalysts, has been tightening over a delay in the Japan-Russia talks.
Gold futures ranged from three to nine yen per gram firmer, with benchmark December ending up six yen at 1,367 yen.
Spot gold was lower at $343.90/344.20 at the Tokyo close, against $344.50/345.00 in New York on Friday.
In lacklustre trade, gold futures retreated from early highs, depressed by a dip in bullion prices and the yen"s slight recovery against the dollar.
Platinum prices were weaker on the heels of palladium.
"Platinum turned into negative territory as heavy profit-taking emerged after the benchmark December hit its life-of-contract high in early Tokyo trade," one trader said.
Platinum prices ranged from eight to 14 yen per gram lower, with benchmark December ending down 12 yen at 1,430 yen.
Benchmark December silver was up 0.4 yen at 207.6 yen per 10 grams.--K. Takagi, Tokyo Commodity Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
